what_this_repo_is.summary: AI-assisted framework for scientific software development: incremental Fortran→C++ translation plus code inspection/generation/update and tool-using agent workflows.

docs.description: Package layout, control flow and class hierarchy
Loop mode internals and on-disk artifacts

notes: Bounded mode is a practical constraint layer, not an OS sandbox.
Bounded bash uses an allowlist and rejects shell metacharacters; some commands will fail by design.
The loop task file can extend the bash allowlist via a [tools] bash = [...] TOML section.

If [tools] bash allowlists a python interpreter, python may only run .py scripts under <mem>/scripts, where mem is the [tools] memory layer (default .codescribe/mem); -c, -m, stdin and the REPL are rejected so executed code is kept on disk for provenance.
TOML diagnostic logs include model_response (with model_text and model_reasoning), tool_start (with args and model_text) and tool_end (with output_preview) events for post-run inspection.
Agent hard limits per run: 120 total tool calls, 10 per iteration, 2 repeat-call attempts (read gets 3x). After 3 consecutive all-error iterations the agent is nudged to emit a BLOCKED answer.
Tool outputs are capped at 8000 chars in message history; truncated output includes a paging hint (read(path, offset=N)).

review.toml (review-phase event log) is always written unconditionally. author.toml is cleared and rewritten at the start of each author phase. Both differ from --log, which routes author-phase events to an additional user-specified path.
The review agent has read, glob, write (for review_output.toml) and a bash tool restricted to: ls, stat, pwd, find, grep, head, tail, which, env, rg, git. No edit or arbitrary shell commands.

Loop convergence is harness-decided: an optional [check] command (argv, exit 0 = pass) runs after every author phase; STATUS: COMPLETE only ends the run with a passing check, a clean review needs a passing or absent check, and 2 loops without progress stop the run as stalled (see docs/loop.md#convergence).

Loop task files may list protected files in [tools] protect = [...]. Protected files are reverted after any author bash call that changes them; reviewer-added [[rule]] entries (deny_bash/protect) are enforced by the harness from the next loop (see docs/loop.md).

Reading a media file (image, PDF, video) attaches it as base64 content blocks; images over CODESCRIBE_MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES (default 4 MB) are downscaled, larger PDFs are rejected, only the newest attachment stays inline, and an HTTP 413 from the gateway strips inline media and retries once.

modes.description: Repeated author→review cycles. Cross-loop state is carried in-memory; each cycle starts a fresh agent whose context is injected by the harness. The loop stops when the task is complete (passing [check] plus author COMPLETE or a clean review) or stalled. On-disk artifacts under .codescribe/loop/ are for inspection and crash-resume only.

options.--workdir DIR: Root directory the agent is bounded to (default: cwd)
options.--reason: Enable extended reasoning (adaptive thinking on Anthropic, reasoning_effort=high on OpenAI-compatible backends)
options.--log: Write TOML diagnostic events to the default path: .codescribe/logs/toolusage.toml
options.--verbose/-v: Stream per-iteration tool calls and token usage to stdout
options.--log-path PATH: Write TOML diagnostic events to PATH (implies --log)

modes.description: Single agent session with tools bounded to --workdir. The TASK argument is either a task string or a path to a TOML task file in the same format as loop; the two forms are mutually exclusive. A task file is loaded as prior conversation, is protected from write/edit/bash, and may extend the bash allowlist through its [tools] section.

example_commands: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... code-scribe agent "Fix failing tests" -m anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-6
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... code-scribe agent "Fix failing tests" -m anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-6 --reason
anthropic_quickstart.reasoning_note: Pass --reason to agent or loop to enable reasoning: adaptive thinking on AnthropicModel, reasoning_effort=high on OpenAI-compatible backends. Anthropic thinking blocks are relayed verbatim into the next turn, as the API requires. CODESCRIBE_MODEL_REASONING=1 is also supported for scripting/CI.

environment_variables.name: CODESCRIBE_MODEL
environment_variables.description: Default model name used when -m/--model is omitted (one of the two is required).

environment_variables.name: CODESCRIBE_MAX_TOKENS
environment_variables.description: Maximum output tokens the model may generate per reply. Applies to all backends. Default: 32768.

environment_variables.name: OPENAI_COMP_BASEURL
environment_variables.description: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API (must include /v1). Used by oaic-* models.

environment_variables.name: OPENAI_COMP_PROVIDER
environment_variables.description: Provider label used for routing/auth policy (e.g. ollama, alcf-inference). Used by oaic-* models.

environment_variables.name: OPENAI_COMP_APIKEY
environment_variables.description: API key for the oaic-* client. Some local endpoints accept any placeholder.

environment_variables.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
environment_variables.description: API key for hosted OpenAI models (openai-* prefix).

environment_variables.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
environment_variables.description: API key for Anthropic models (anthropic-* prefix). Required when using the recommended Anthropic backend for agent and loop commands.

environment_variables.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
environment_variables.description: Optional base URL override for Anthropic models (e.g. a proxy endpoint).

environment_variables.name: CODESCRIBE_MODEL_REASONING
environment_variables.description: Set to '1' to enable reasoning on every backend (adaptive thinking on Anthropic, reasoning_effort=high on OpenAI-compatible).

environment_variables.name: CODESCRIBE_MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES
environment_variables.description: Largest media file (raw bytes) inlined as base64 per request; larger images are downscaled. Default: 4000000.

model_setup.recommended: Anthropic (anthropic-*) for agent and loop commands — native tool calling, streaming, and adaptive reasoning are all supported. Use oaic-* for local or OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
model_setup.example_command: code-scribe inspect README.rst -m oaic-llama3.1 -q "Summarize this repo and list key entry points."
